title: Why Are There So Few Trash Cans in Japan
paragraphs: Japan is famous for its clean streets. But many visitors are surprised to find that there are very few public trash cans. So why are trash cans so hard to find in Japan?

One important reason is safety. In 1995, members of a group called Aum Shinrikyo released a deadly nerve gas called sarin on the Tokyo subway. After this attack, many public trash cans, especially in train stations, were removed so that dangerous objects could not be hidden in them. In fact, according to one report, one of the containers of nerve gas used in the attack was hidden in a trash can. Since then, having few trash cans has become normal.

Another reason is money. According to a tourism professor at Temple University's campus in Japan, cuts to budgets have also played a part, since collecting and managing trash from public bins costs money.

Culture also plays a big role. In Japan, many people believe that they are responsible for their own trash. Instead of throwing it away in public, people often carry their trash in a bag or in their pocket and take it home.

Japan also has strict rules about sorting trash. People must separate it into different types, such as things that can be burned, plastics, plastic bottles, cans and glass. The rules can be different in each city or town. Some people prefer to sort their trash at home, so they do not make mistakes.

However, there are still some places where people can throw away trash. Convenience stores often have trash cans outside. Many vending machines also have special bins next to them, but these are only for bottles and cans bought from that machine.
Recently, some places in Japan have started to put trash cans back in public areas, partly because of the large number of tourists.
